grade.first_issue: In Case 3, the proof does not justify the jump from the orbit-exclusion observations to the structural assertion that S_0=(0,b] and S_{c_1}=(b,∞). Boundedness of S_0 alone does not imply this, and the statement that an orbit tending to infinity must start to the right of a forbidden interval omits the necessary no-jumping argument and quantifier clarification.
grade.summary: The proposed family f(x)=x+c is verified correctly. The identities g(f(y))=g(y), the iterate formula, and g≥0 are correct, and the argument excluding two distinct positive values of g is essentially sound. The remaining mixed-value case contains a load-bearing gap: the interval structure and boundary membership of the two level sets are asserted rather than proved. This is nevertheless a localized repair using ideas already present: start the first orbit argument at an arbitrary p∈S_{c_1}; since its forbidden interval has length greater than c_1, obtain p>z for every z∈S_0. This gives an initial/final cut, after which both possible assignments of the boundary are contradicted by the displayed inequalities. Under Rule F this merits 5 rather than full credit; the required repair is bounded but not written.
strengths: Correctly verifies every function f(x)=x+c with c≥0 by RMS-AM-GM.
Correctly derives f(f(y))=2f(y)-y, invariance of g along forward orbits, and nonnegativity of g.
The comparison of two positive defect values uses the right squared inequalities and a valid bounded-distance orbit strategy.
The mixed-value case introduces a promising forbidden-interval argument that contains the core idea needed for repair.

errors.description: The mixed zero/positive defect case relies on an unproved structural conclusion about the level sets. The proof must explicitly apply the orbit argument to every positive-defect starting point, derive the global ordering of the two sets, and handle both possible memberships of the cut point.
